title: Role of epinephrine-mediated beta-adrenergic mechanisms in hypoglycemic glucose counterregulation and posthypoglycemic hyperglycemia in insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus
authors: Popp DA, Shah SD, Cryer PE
population: Eight patients with insulin-dependent diabetes (mean age 28 years, without symptomatic autonomic neuropathy) and seven non-diabetic controls at the Washington University Clinical Research Center
funder: This study was supported by U.S. Public Health Service grants AM 27085, RR 00036 and AM 20579.
result: After intravenous regular insulin 0.075 U/kg, glucose recovery from hypoglycaemia during propranolol infusion was compared with saline. In non-diabetic controls beta-adrenergic blockade left glucose counterregulation unaffected. In patients with insulin-dependent diabetes, whose glucagon responses to hypoglycaemia were markedly diminished, glucose recovery was significantly impaired during blockade, and posthypoglycaemic hyperglycaemia was prevented; the dependence on adrenaline-mediated beta-adrenergic mechanisms varied inversely with residual glucagon secretion.
